summary: Excessive creation of temporary tables on disk in MySQL, despite configuration adjustments.
symptoms: High percentage of temporary tables created on disk.
Performance concerns related to disk-based temporary tables.
mechanism: Implicit temporary tables exceeding memory limits or involving unsupported data types (e.g., TEXT/BLOB).

facts.evidence: Post mentions configuration changes to reduce disk-based temp tables.

facts.key: TEXT/BLOB fields force disk-based temp tables
facts.evidence: Answer 1 explains MEMORY engine limitations with TEXT/BLOB fields.

facts.key: Queries with GROUP BY or ORDER BY may create temp tables
facts.evidence: Post and answers discuss query patterns causing temp tables.

assumptions: The database schema includes TEXT/BLOB fields or large columns.
Queries involve GROUP BY, ORDER BY, or UNION operations.
unknowns: Exact schema and query workload causing temp table creation.
Whether other configuration settings contribute to the issue.
